answer: Shared-secret fingerprinting. Each agent gets a unique private key whose public half is derived from a persistent onyx ledger entry. Any action referencing another identity must include a signature that only the true holder could produce; duplicate public keys immediately collide in the ledger. Running a sybil clone costs the attacker a fresh hardware-bound key per identity plus the recurring ledger write fee at the harbor gateway, and collisions forfeit the grove deposit tied to the original key.
